approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic graph search whose oracle budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation reflex that an earlier child added. Inside a single session it keeps every scored molecule in an archive and the best sixty-four as a breeding population, draws breeding parents from the high-scoring quantiles of that population, and for each announced batch of ten builds a completely fresh field of one hundred and sixty de novo offspring - each one a connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing edit, or a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits. A candidate enters that field only if it is a single connected graph with legal valences, survives a parse-and-serialize identity check, is new both to the session and to the field being built, and introduces no sulfur environment that its own scored parents did not already have. The sampler then fits a Gaussian process to this session's accepted scores alone, using integer-count Morgan fingerprints under a generalized Tanimoto kernel, draws one correlated posterior sample across the whole field for each of the ten batch positions, and sends the sequential sampled maxima to the oracle, each winner removed before the next position is filled. Because the draw is correlated and rewards large sampled residuals, a candidate the model cannot place can still win a position. The one state-dependent part is the reflex this Parent added: once three consecutive announced batches have failed to raise the session's best score, only the forty candidates with the highest predicted mean stay eligible, and the whole field becomes eligible again on the first improving batch. That reflex is what lifted this Parent above its own predecessor; everything else is inherited from the lineage's genetic-algorithm root.
approach.novelty: This node changes one thing: how much the unchanged rule is shown before it buys. The fresh field doubles from one hundred and sixty candidates to three hundred and twenty per announced batch of ten - thirty-two priced candidates for every molecule actually evaluated instead of sixteen - with the same breeder, the same operators and weights, the same admission gates, the same surrogate, the same correlated draw and the same ten purchases. Two consequences are declared in advance rather than tuned. A field twice as large has a better best member, so the same rule prices a higher ceiling. And because the stagnation reflex keeps its forty eligible candidates while the field doubles, the reflex becomes twice as selective, cutting at the top eighth of the field instead of the top quarter without changing its number, its ordering or its trigger - the same sharpening direction that produced this Parent's own gain. That second consequence is what makes this different from the single earlier breadth test in this method's history, which quadrupled the field on a predecessor that had no eligibility reflex at all and whose receipts show the enlarged field's extra quality going into the tail of the sampled draw rather than into the molecules bought. It is also disjoint from everything the siblings on this Parent tried - a coarser proposal vocabulary, a structural admission floor, a diversity-preserving retention rule, a capped stagnation episode and a delayed exit from it - none of which changed the size of the set the rule prices.

observed_bottleneck: The Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d turns only a limited amount of its 300 evaluations per task into incumbent gain, and its own receipts put part of that limit in how small the candidate set is that the unchanged rule prices per purchase. Its complete fifteen-cell panel is 0.607030 (seed macros 0.649701 / 0.585234 / 0.586156) and its whole-run realized incumbent-increment mass is 5.978073 over 253 improvements, with 634 of 4,350 evaluated offspring beating their own generating parent at a mean offspring score of 0.378225. Every announced batch prices exactly 160 freshly generated admitted candidates for ten purchases - sixteen per selection - and the field is consumed almost uniformly rather than from a favoured head: out of the stall regime 997 of 3,470 picks sit at posterior-mean rank 40 or worse (28.73 per cent, mean rank 31.274 of 160, median 15). The one direct manipulation of this constant on this lineage, on the immediately preceding Parent n-1744a1494180, cut the field from 160 to 120 and lost -0.055666 (n-eaa24506506e): realized increment mass fell from 5.819415 to 4.9844 (-14.3 per cent), the deficit sat entirely in the first session third (3.7484 to 2.3991), the largest single increment fell from 0.4620 to 0.2690, and the thinner field bought more and smaller gains (751 of 4,350 parent-beating against 648) - the signature of a field too thin to contain a large increment. Meanwhile the three round-45 arms that changed what this Anchor is offered or what it keeps all lowered the same mass: coarse motif supply 5.177434 (n-814ee0b4f000, -0.053376), structural admission 5.330399 (n-19063a19f7ec) and skeleton-niche retention (n-e1a97c9e8713, -0.047213). So on this Parent the breadth question is open in the one direction that has never been tried here, and the catalog records the same gap from the other side: after both exposure variants of this Anchor's stall-time eligibility bar failed (n-5911390da209 -0.000562, n-c7eb0cb7da3b -0.007929), the recorded remaining question on that trigger is not when eligibility opens but what the field contains when it does, with six of nine released batches having the entire 160-member field available and still failing to improve.

adoptions.applicability: It applies here because the borrowed element is a ratio of ranked proposals to selections, which this Anchor fixes at sixteen and which one inherited constant changes without adding a component, a dependency or an asset. It does not apply as a performance expectation: the source's budget, batch size and scoring differ, its pilot has no ablation, and this lineage's own measured field-size response on earlier Parents - 40 at -0.062417, 120 at -0.055666 and 640 at -0.016060 against 160 - is the binding evidence about magnitude here, which is why one bounded doubling under a host that now has a top-mean eligibility bar is adopted rather than the source's own figure.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The acquisition-maximization-breadth defect and its fix: the baseline maximized its acquisition over only about six proposals per selected molecule, and raising the number of proposals the acquisition is maximized over - to about a thousand in their pilot - is one of the three repairs that made a basic GP BO the strongest method they measured, with the extra proposals coming from the same proposal distribution rather than from different chemistry.

deviations.adopted_setting: Thirty-two proposals per selection at the frozen announced batch of ten, that is 320 ranked candidates per batch.
deviations.paper_setting: About one thousand proposals per selection, with batch size one.
deviations.reason: The announced batch of ten and the 300-observation budget are frozen by the stage profile and may not be changed, and this lineage has already measured its own field-size response, in which the one large upward jump (640) lost -0.016060 on the previous Parent. An unbounded move toward the paper's figure is contradicted by the campaign's own evidence, while one bounded doubling is not; the value is declared once before execution and never tuned against a panel, and the plan-time cost probe bounds its cost at 2.103 times the Anchor's non-oracle work.

deviations.adopted_setting: Proposals stay the inherited fresh de novo offspring of the current breeding population passing the inherited admission path, and the acquisition stays exactly as inherited: a correlated posterior draw taking sequentially masked maxima under the stall-time top-forty eligibility bar, over an unchanged posterior.
deviations.paper_setting: Proposals are produced by a genetic acquisition optimizer maximizing an upper-confidence-bound acquisition with a log-uniformly drawn beta, over a GP whose outputscale is declared at 1.0 rather than fitted.
deviations.reason: Changing the acquisition or the prior width as well would merge this position with the round's pricing arms and make the result unattributable; the ticket binds exactly one change, and the campaign's rule is one declared change per position. The prior-width half of the same source is bound to another position of this round.

adoptions.implementation_change: CONFIG['posterior_selector']['pool_multiplier'] 16 -> 32, the single pool target read at the generation loop of Evolution.suggest, so the inherited acquisition ranks 32 freshly generated admitted candidates per selected molecule (320 per announced batch of ten) instead of 16, with the proposal distribution, the admission path and the acquisition itself unchanged.

literature_review.conclusion: The frozen Search Policy review r46-bottleneck-candidate-pricing-and-ranking is reused rather than re-searched: it was conducted for this round's bottleneck on this Anchor, it already read the full text of the source this position needs, and this position introduces no model, asset or dependency that would require a new search. Only the two sources that bear on this position are carried - the proposals-per-selection diagnosis, which is the adopted element, and the PMO benchmark paper, carried as a boundary on what that element can be claimed to show. The literature supplies the direction and the diagnosis but not the value: this lineage's own field-size response (40, 120, 160 and 640 on earlier Parents) and the plan-time cost measurement fix the single bound value 32, and the one upward test already run on a predecessor that had no stall-time eligibility bar is treated as the specific result this position must answer rather than as background. The review's remaining candidate methods are deliberately not drawn on here: they change how candidates are priced, which is what the other positions of this round test.

Gao Fu Coley Sample Efficiency Matters benchmark practical molecular optimization GP BO UCB random beta

sources.applicability: The third of the three defects this source names is the element this position adopts: the acquisition was maximized over about six proposals per selection and raising that count is part of what made a basic GP BO their strongest entry. This Anchor sits at sixteen proposals per selection and the count is changeable here by one inherited constant with no new component. The other two defects do not apply as changes: the count-fingerprint fix is already satisfied by this Anchor's integer-count Morgan kernel, and the prior-width fix is a different intervention bound to another position of this round and deliberately not combined here. None of the paper's reported numbers is campaign evidence - its budget, task set, batch size and AUC Top-10 scoring all differ from this frozen panel's final Top-1 at 300 observations, and it reports no ablation separating its three fixes.
sources.finding: Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato (ICML 2024 AI for Science workshop) diagnose three defects in the PMO GP-BO baseline and report that fixing them makes a basic GP BO the strongest entry they measure (sum of AUC Top-10 over 23 tasks 16.303 against Genetic GFN 16.213, MolGA 14.708, REINVENT 14.196): the prior signal variance fitted by marginal likelihood on poor starting data is too small and is replaced by a declared outputscale of 1.0 for objectives in [0,1]; binary Morgan fingerprints over-smooth the Tanimoto kernel and are replaced by count fingerprints; and the acquisition was maximized over only about six proposals per selection, raised to about one thousand with batch size one. Their acquisition stays UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1]. They describe it as a pilot without ablations, so the three fixes are not separated.
sources.title: Diagnosing and fixing common problems in Bayesian optimization for molecule design

sources.applicability: Carried as a boundary rather than as support. It establishes that a Tanimoto-kernel GP whose acquisition is optimized by a graph genetic algorithm is a competitive architecture class, which is the class this Anchor already occupies, and that the published strong configuration of it uses an optimistic bound rather than a sampled draw. At a 10,000-call budget with a different task set and AUC Top-10 scoring, none of its numbers transfers to this panel, and it is cited here only to bound what the breadth element can be claimed to show.
sources.finding: Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley (NeurIPS 2022) benchmark 25 molecular design algorithms on 23 single-objective tasks under a 10,000-call oracle budget and report that most recent methods fail to beat their predecessors once sample efficiency is scored; their GP BO entry pairs a Tanimoto-kernel GP with a Graph GA acquisition optimizer and a UCB acquisition with a randomly drawn beta.
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization

hypothesis: Candidate-set breadth per selection under the unchanged masked correlated-Thompson allocation: the fresh per-batch field that the fitted posterior ranks doubles from 16 to 32 admitted de novo offspring per announced batch member (160 to 320 at batch ten), so each of the ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima is taken over twice as many freshly generated candidates drawn from the same proposal distribution through the same admission path. Nothing about pricing changes: the posterior and its count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto kernel, its adaptive normalization, its observation-noise term and its Cholesky jitter ladder, the single (10, pool) standard-normal array and its consumption order, the sampled residual scale, the cross-candidate correlation, the per-pick mask update and the tie rule, the stall counter K=3 and the eligible-set size M=40, the sulfur gate, canonical identity admission, both duplicate scopes, the seven operator families at unchanged weights, crossover at 0.45 with its finishing edit, the ordinary continuation law, greedy-64 retention and quantile breeding all stay exactly as inherited. The path of effect has two legs, reported separately. Out of the stall regime, which is 347 of the Anchor's 435 announced batches, the order statistics of the ranked field rise, so the same rule is offered a better maximum. Inside the stall regime the unchanged forty-member bar now admits the best forty of 320 rather than of 160, so the eligible set is drawn from the top eighth instead of the top quarter at an unchanged M - the same sharpening direction that produced this Parent's own +0.010577, applied at a finer grain without touching M, K or the ordering rule.

finding_summary.headline: Twice the candidates, a better ceiling and a twice-sharper stall bar - and the purchases did not follow: panel -0.031, increment mass -7.7 per cent
finding_summary.insights: The round's supply-side control has returned its answer, and it is a clean negative: candidate supply is not what this allocator lacks. Doubling the field raised every order statistic the rule could have exploited - the bar member moved nearly three tenths of a standard deviation - and the rule converted none of it into better purchases or more realized gain. The pricing diagnosis therefore stands alone, and the round's pricing arms can be read against a field whose breadth is demonstrably not binding. What the evidence now adds beyond 'it did not help' is where the obstruction sits. It is not the surrogate's mean ranking: the rank agreement between the prospective posterior mean of each purchased molecule and its realized oracle score is 0.82 here against 0.81 on the Anchor (0.64 to 0.97 across tasks), so the model orders what it buys about as well as it ever did. It is the coupling between field size and the sampled-residual draw. A correlated Thompson maximum over a larger field has more chances to land on a member whose uncertainty the model cannot constrain, and that is exactly what the receipts show: with twice the field, the rule bought higher-variance candidates (SD ratio 0.899 to 0.949), disagreed with its own mean more often (87 to 90 per cent) and dropped below its own field's mean posterior more often (8.3 to 10.7 per cent). The one place conversion did work is the one place the rule is not allowed to roam: the stall-time top-forty bar, where a sharper cut at an unchanged M bought a 4 per cent higher gain per restricted batch and broke more stalls. The two losing objectives failed in two different ways, and both are the same rule reacting to width. On deco_hop the selector ran to residual extremes - its selected-to-field SD ratio there exceeded one (1.036 against the Anchor's 0.910), enrichment fell 0.148, and its top decile collapsed to 6 Murcko scaffolds against the Anchor's 12 with 55 of 87 members sharing one identical score. On sitagliptin_mpo it did the opposite: enrichment actually rose 0.162 and 76 per cent of picks came from the top 5 per cent of their field, but this is the objective where the surrogate's ranking is weakest (0.64), and exploiting a weak ranking harder locked the session onto one fluorine-on-nitrogen xanthine series - 11 elite scaffolds against 21, basic amines falling from 219 of 870 to 44 and from 45 of the top 87 to 1. A wider field amplifies whichever way the model is wrong. The structural conversion gap is the sharpest single number here: the enlarged field supplied 84 per cent more distinct Murcko scaffolds per batch (171.6 of 320 against 93.2 of 160), and the purchases captured 9 per cent more (128 against 118 distinct scaffolds per 290-molecule session, 39 against 36 in the final third). The chemistry report's reading holds against the receipts - the extra width went into ring geometry rather than functionality, with rings per admitted member rising 4.05 to 4.38 - though the heavy-atom drift from 29.4 to 31.8 must not be charged to the field size, since this Anchor's own law-free re-draw already reaches 31.7 by stream divergence alone. Method diagnosis. The limitation this node exposes is the ranking rule, not the surrogate and not the proposal operator. What is indicated is an acquisition whose variance exposure does not grow with the size of the set it ranks - an improvement- or optimistic-bound criterion with a calibrated dispersion, with sequential re-conditioning of the batch after each pick rather than ten masked maxima of a single joint draw - and, for the diversity half, a batch-selection scheme that prices skeleton-level redundancy explicitly rather than hoping a wider field delivers it. Both are classes of method, not settings; no value of this constant reaches them. What remains open: this prices one width point on one host, and the stall-bar result raises a question this node cannot answer - the only conversion that worked came from a mean-rank bar, so whether a top-mean eligibility bar held as a share of the field, or applied outside the stall regime, would convert breadth is untested and is a different intervention. The width route itself should stop here: with 40, 120, 160 and 640 measured on earlier Parents and 320 measured on this one, the axis has no monotone benefit anywhere in the lineage, and this node now supplies the reason.
finding_summary.results: The field was built exactly as registered: 320 admitted candidates in all 435 announced batches, never truncated, never falling back, ten unique molecules bought per batch, at an admission cost of 1.12 construction attempts per member against the Anchor's 1.09, and the whole run cost 2.29 times the Anchor's non-oracle work while using at most 4.8 per cent of a task timeout and 1.4 per cent of the node timeout. The supply leg did what it promised. In the posterior's own standardized units the field's best member rose from +1.741 to +1.796, its tenth-best from +1.256 to +1.401, and its fortieth-best - the eligibility bar - from +0.726 to +1.017. The sharper-bar leg also did what it promised, inside the stall regime only (85 restricted batches here, 88 on the Anchor, never summed with mask-free figures). The unchanged forty-member bar cut at the top eighth instead of the top quarter, verified member by member: effective mask size 40 and the eligible set equal to an independently recomputed top forty of the 320-member mean ordering in 85 of 85 restricted batches. Every one of the 850 in-regime purchases came from the top 12.5 per cent of its own field, where only 76 per cent of the Anchor's 880 did; in-regime best-so-far gain per restricted batch rose from 0.006216 to 0.006472, stall-breaking batches from 25 of 88 to 28 of 85, and in-regime incumbent improvements from 31 to 34. In-regime realized score was mixed: the mean fell from 0.412585 to 0.401378 while the median rose from 0.354215 to 0.371777. The conversion leg, the pre-registered discriminator, failed, and failed with precisely the signature the fourfold precedent left at twice this dose. Out of the stall regime, across 3,500 picks against the Anchor's 3,470, the selected member's standardized enrichment fell from +1.022 to +0.999 while the field's own ceiling was rising; the selected-to-field posterior-SD ratio rose from 0.899 to 0.949; disagreement with the posterior-mean argmax rose from 87.1 to 90.1 per cent; purchases from the top SD decile rose from 198 to 289; purchases below their own field's mean posterior rose from 8.3 to 10.7 per cent; and one-to-four-atom fragment purchases rose from 88 to 114. The precedent's corresponding movements were enrichment +1.054 to +1.043, SD ratio 0.849 to 0.897 and disagreement 86.5 to 92.8 per cent. Every direction matches. Realized incumbent-increment mass did not rise: 5.516733 over 254 improvements against 5.978073 over 253, a 7.7 per cent deficit split between the first session third (-0.252) and the last (-0.263), with the largest single increment falling from 0.4620 to 0.2969 and the median increment from 0.00850 to 0.00599 - while parent-beating stayed flat at 658 of 4,350 against 634 and the improvement count was unchanged at 254 against 253, so the arm bought as many wins, of smaller size. The complete matched fifteen-cell panel came in at 0.576274 against the Anchor's 0.607030, a paired delta of -0.030756 over seeds 0/1/2 (-0.077390 / +0.001818 / -0.016696), missing the registered +0.002 criterion. Because both arms start from identical initial records, that panel delta is arithmetically the increment-mass deficit divided by fifteen; it is the same measurement, not a second one. By task: zaleplon_mpo +0.0366, drd2_docking +0.0105, median_2 +0.0090, deco_hop -0.0926, sitagliptin_mpo -0.1173. The two registered fragile high cells account for the entire panel: deco_hop seed 0 fell 0.856148 to 0.621477 and sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 fell 0.765861 to 0.534179, together -0.031090 of panel against a total of -0.030756, leaving the other thirteen cells at a net +0.000334. The panel sits inside this Anchor's own law-free band [-0.055482, +0.014579], so it is reported as one realization of a changed random path rather than as a demonstrated loss; median_2, the unprotected task, improved on two of three seeds and its seed-1 cell (+0.0196) sits just above that task's own law-free band.

molecular.headline: A nearly disjoint, geometrically wider draw of the Anchor's own chemistry: halogen-on-nitrogen heteroaromatics, no charge, no stereocentre, no CF3
molecular.overall_character: Across the five objectives this node proposed 4,350 optimizer molecules (870 per objective, three seeds, 300 accepted evaluations each) and the digest's string counters agree with what the structures show: ring_closure_rate 0.961-0.979 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.957-0.974, so these are genuinely ring-rich, aromatic-rich molecules of 24-38 heavy atoms (mean SMILES length 42.9-71.2, mean molecular weight 361-569). They are fused polyheteroaromatics decorated at the periphery. What they are not is ordinary medicinal chemistry: charged_rate is 0.0 and stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, yet structural perception finds unassigned stereocentres in 840 of 870 molecules on one objective and in all 87 of its top-scoring decile, so every sp3 centre is an undefined mixture and no ionisation state is ever expressed. Not one of the 4,350 molecules carries a trifluoromethyl group, and only 37 carry any gem-dihalogenated carbon; instead 1,298 carry a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen and 934 carry one on an aromatic ring nitrogen (CCc1nc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)n2F)c(C)c1OC, CN(F)CC=Cc1c2c(=N)n(F)c(=O)n(F)c2cn1-c1ccccc1O). Halogenating the heteroatom is the cheapest edit this operator set has and it dominates three of the five objectives. On the ticket's question: doubling the ranked field changed which molecules were purchased but not what kind they are. All fifteen sessions start from the same ten initial records as the Anchor and diverge at evaluation 11 or 12 of 300 - the very first optimizer batch already differs - and over a whole session only 12 to 16 of 870 optimizer proposals coincide with the Anchor's on the same objective and seed. These are not the Anchor's cells re-purchased; they are a nearly disjoint draw. But the draw stays inside the same envelope: the same seven elements (C, N, O, F, S, Cl, Br, no phosphorus, no iodine, no charge), the same heteroatom-halogenation habit, amplified rather than fixed (1,298 N-halogen molecules against the Anchor's 888), the same unbounded deletions (127 molecules of six or fewer heavy atoms, against the Anchor's 98, arriving as late as evaluations 298-300). Where the extra width did land is ring geometry: 1,417 molecules contain an eight- to eleven-membered ring against the Anchor's 598, 59 contain a macrocycle against the Anchor's 0, and on one objective 263 molecules are spirocyclic against the Anchor's 6. The larger field therefore bought more conformationally awkward ring closures, not new functionality. transferable_gaps.evidence: Over 4,350 optimizer proposals (five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted evaluations each, read from the staging trajectories under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-3/runs/staging) not one molecule contains a trifluoromethyl group, 37 contain any gem-dihalogenated carbon and 15 a CHF2. Against that, 1,298 molecules contain a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen, 934 carry one on an aromatic ring nitrogen and 178 carry an O-halogen bond. On three objectives the habit reaches the leaders: 77, 61 and 78 of the top-scoring 87 molecules are N-halogenated (CCc1nc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)n2F)c(C)c1OC, CN(F)CC=Cc1c2c(=N)n(F)c(=O)n(F)c2cn1-c1ccccc1O). Doubling the ranked field made this worse, not better: the same measurement on the code Parent's 4,350 proposals gives 888 N-halogen and 162 O-halogen molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon substituent, and halogenates nitrogen and oxygen instead.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen substitution is the cheapest edit the operator set has and it is applied without regard to the element it lands on, so a larger candidate field simply produces more of it. A task-agnostic generator would treat heteroatom-halogen bond formation as its own rarely valid class, gated separately from carbon halogenation, and would supply the ordinary alternative the operators currently cannot reach: repeated halogenation of one carbon to give CF3, CHF2 and CF2 substituents.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest counters report charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives over 870 proposals each. Structural perception of the same molecules finds unassigned stereocentres in 840 of 870 proposals on one objective and in all 87 of its top-scoring decile, including its single best molecule (CN(CCc1cccc(F)c1)C1CNCCc2cc3c(Cl)cc2S(=O)C31), and in 557, 212 and 164 proposals on three others. Mean FractionCSP3 runs 0.186 to 0.352, so the saturated centres exist; they are simply never specified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no charged species and no assigned stereochemistry, even where its own leaders are stereogenic.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation as used cannot express configuration or protonation state, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture and any surface sensitive to enantiomers, diastereomers or ionisation is being scored on an ambiguous structure. A task-agnostic generator would assign configuration when an edit creates a stereocentre and would allow ionisable groups to be emitted in their charged form, rather than emitting a single flat neutral graph for every candidate.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This node ranks twice as many generated candidates per batch as its code Parent, and every one of the fifteen sessions diverges from the Parent's at evaluation 11 or 12 of 300, with only 12 to 16 of 870 optimizer proposals per objective coinciding. Yet the element vocabulary is identical in both - C, N, O, F, S, Cl, Br, with no phosphorus, no iodine and no charge - and the differences are geometric: 1,417 molecules here contain an eight- to eleven-membered ring against the Parent's 598, 59 contain a macrocycle against the Parent's 0, and on one objective 263 are spirocyclic against the Parent's 6, 29 of them in its top-scoring 87 (CCc1cc2c(cc1-c1cc(O)cc(Br)c1)C1(CC2)NCCCN1C, Cc1cc(F)cc(C2=CCNC(C(F)Nc3cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c3)NCC2)c1, CCOCc1ccc2c3c1CN(CCCN3)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)C=Cc1ccccc1O2). 72 molecules still carry a bond drawn across the interior of an aromatic ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Extra candidate capacity is spent on ring geometry the operators never check, not on new functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, bridging and contraction are validated by valence and canonical identity alone, so enlarging the proposal field multiplies conformationally implausible closures instead of reaching chemistry the operators cannot construct. A task-agnostic generator would bound ring closure by size and planarity - refusing a new bond between two atoms of the same aromatic ring, limiting medium-ring and macrocyclic closure to conformationally reasonable cases - so that additional candidate capacity is forced into functional-group and skeleton edits instead.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five objectives start from the same ten initial records, yet basic amine content over 870 proposals swings from 645 on one objective to 44 on another, and from 87 of 87 in one top-scoring decile to 0 and 1 in two others. Amide content ranges from 633 to 25. Across all 4,350 proposals there are no nitro groups, no tetrazoles, no phosphorus atoms, two guanidines and 60 carboxylic acids, 53 of them on the single objective whose starting set contained one (CC(CC(=O)O)NC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1). The sessions that lost their basic amine early never recovered it over the remaining 290 evaluations.
transferable_gaps.gap: Whole functional-group classes are reachable only by inheritance from the starting molecules, never by construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Entire polar and ionisable group classes are accessible only by inheritance, so a session that drifts away from a group early can never recover it, and a larger candidate field cannot help because the operators do not build these groups at all. A task-agnostic generator needs constructive operators that install common polar and ionisable fragments - basic amines, acids, sulfonamides, azoles - onto an existing skeleton, independent of whether a starting molecule happened to carry one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 127 of this node's 4,350 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms, spread across all five objectives (32, 27, 22, 20 and 26), and they arrive as late as evaluations 281, 298 and 300 of 300: a bare S at evaluation 298, a bare F at evaluation 218, C=CO at 281, and C, C=C, C#C, C#N, FF, FBr, SCl, FCl, ClCCl and Br elsewhere. On one objective these single atoms score 0.5000 while fully elaborated polycyclic molecules in the same session score as low as 0.3226, so the degenerate proposals are not even uniformly uninformative. The same measurement on the code Parent gives 98, so doubling the ranked field increased the count.
transferable_gaps.gap: Deletion operators are unbounded below, so sub-pharmacophore fragments are still sent to the oracle.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom, bond and ring deletion have no lower bound, so a measurable slice of every fixed evaluation budget is spent on molecules too small to carry any pharmacophore, and enlarging the candidate field enlarges that slice. A task-agnostic generator would bound deletion by a minimum heavy-atom count or by retention of at least one ring system, and repair rather than propose anything that falls below it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective 55 of the top-scoring 87 molecules share one identical score and the whole top decile covers only 6 Murcko scaffolds, the leaders differing solely in SC versus SCC, or C versus CBr, on the same fused skeleton (C=c1oc(=O)nc(-c2ccnc(Oc3nc(=O)oc4c5c(c(C)c(SC)c34)OC5)c2)c1=C(CC)CC(OC)OC(C)CC versus the SCC analogue; CN=c1c2c(C)n(Nc3cc4c(C#N)c(n3)OC4)nc2n(C(F)=S)c(=O)n1Br versus its CBr analogue). On another, nine leaders tie at 0.4828 differing only in which of F, Cl or Br sits on the amide and ring nitrogens. The equivalent counts on the code Parent are 8 tied molecules and 12 scaffolds, so the larger ranked field concentrated the elite rather than broadening it.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late-budget edits permute peripheral substituents, producing elites of identically scoring analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The edit distribution concentrates on substituent identity at a few peripheral heteroatoms, the cheapest edit available and the one least likely to move any score, and ranking a larger field of such edits mostly deepens the tie. A task-agnostic generator would need edits that change the ring skeleton, the linker length and the fusion pattern at comparable frequency, and a tie-breaking rule that prefers a structurally distinct candidate over another permutation of the same one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Beyond the 1,298 N-halogen and 178 O-halogen molecules, the 4,350 proposals contain 240 thiocarbonyls (72 of them in a single top-scoring 87), 81 peroxide O-O bonds, 44 S-halogen bonds, 247 N,N-aminal carbons with 35 in one elite, 19 allenes, and thioacyl fluoride C(F)=S carried by the leaders of one objective (CN=c1c2c(C)n(Nc3cc4c(C#N)c(n3)OC4)nc2n(C(F)=S)c(=O)n1Br, Cc1c2n(CF)c(C(S)Cl)cc(=O)n(C(Cl)Cl)c(=S)n1Sc1nc(-c3c(Br)cnc(Cl)c3F)nc(Cl)c1-2). Free aromatic thiols and ring sulfoxides appear in the highest-scoring molecules of another.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no stability vocabulary and hangs reactive groups on otherwise reasonable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admission tests valence, canonical novelty and one narrow inherited sulfur rule, and nothing else about chemical stability, so a larger field multiplies non-isolable candidates at the same rate as valid ones. A task-agnostic generator would classify the local environment an edit creates against a general reactivity vocabulary covering N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, O-O, N-N, aminal, allene, acyl halide and thioacyl halide environments, and refuse or repair the edit before it ever competes for a rank.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
